sections.heading: Vision and mission
sections.intro: The vision defines the society SBWPC seeks while the mission describes how the organization works toward that goal

cards.title: The society we seek
cards.body: To achieve a society based upon the feminist values of social, political, racial and economic gender equality

cards.title: How we work toward that vision
cards.body:
As a nonpartisan political action committee, we endorse candidates who support our positions and promote a feminist agenda. We are committed to taking social action against discrimination based on gender, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, age or ability

To promote and fund these goals, we provide Candidate Development Workshops, Endorsement Meetings, Cosmopolitics, Presidents’ Circle Luncheons, Community Outreach events and Educational Forums

images.alt: An SBWPC volunteer greets a visitor at the SBWPC table at a community event

hero.heading: A legacy of feminist political leadership
hero.body: Since 1987, the Santa Barbara Women’s Political Committee has brought women together to build political power, advance equality and create pathways into public leadership throughout Santa Barbara County

sections.heading: Three women started a political network
sections.intro: Gayle Binion, Lois Phillips and Susan Rose began organizing in 1987 by calling people they believed would care about feminist political action in Santa Barbara

image.alt: Historical image from the SBWPC archive

children.text: SBWPC’s first public event brought feminist author and National Organization for Women co-founder Betty Friedan to a reception at Zelo’s restaurant on State Street
That gathering established a tradition that still defines SBWPC: connecting people, ideas and political action in one room
“They each called people they thought might be interested, those people called other people, and Santa Barbara may never be the same again”

sections.heading: The women who set it in motion
sections.intro: The organization began through personal relationships, persistence and a shared belief that women needed greater political access, voice and power

hero.heading: Invest in a feminist future
hero.subheading: A Fund for a Feminist Future
hero.body: This dedicated SBWPC fund helps feminist women gain the skills, resources and support needed to run for office, seek appointments and lead where public decisions are made

image.alt: Two SBWPC members in equality shirts holding No Kings and Protect Democracy signs

sections.heading: More feminist women where decisions are made
sections.intro: Increase the number of feminist women in elected and appointed office and in other positions where policies affecting women and families are discussed, shaped and enacted

sections.heading: Two ways to invest in feminist leadership

cards.title: Training Scholarships
cards.body: Scholarships help qualified SBWPC women members attend training programs and develop the skills needed to conduct effective political campaigns or pursue appointed public office

cards.title: Campaign Support
cards.body: The fund also contributes to the campaigns of feminist women candidates who have been endorsed by SBWPC

sections.heading: Prepare for the next level of public leadership
sections.intro: Scholarship requests describe the training program, the applicant’s political goals and how the opportunity will strengthen future public leadership

children.text: Review the requirements before you apply
The complete scholarship requirements are available in one concise view

sections.heading: What to include
sections.intro: Receiving a scholarship does not guarantee endorsement by SBWPC · Applications may also be mailed to SBWPC, P.O. Box 90618, Santa Barbara, CA 93190-0618

items.title: Training program information
items.body: Identify the campaign or public-leadership training program you wish to attend and provide the relevant program details

items.title: Current résumé
items.body: Include a current résumé that outlines your education, work, community involvement and political engagement

items.title: Personal statement
items.body: Address your political goals, commitment to feminist values, what you hope to gain from the training and how you plan to use it

items.title: Two letters of recommendation
items.body: Recommendations should come from people who can speak to your political engagement, feminist commitment and potential for effective public leadership

items.title: Review and possible interview
items.body: The President and the chairs of Fund Development and Candidate Development review applications and an interview may be scheduled
